domain: The taxonomic homelessness of the prompter's craft — is writing effective instructions for AI systems a form of programming, writing, translation, or something none of these names fit?
topic: The taxonomic homelessness of the prompter's craft — is writing effective instructions for AI systems a form of programming, writing, translation, or something none of these names fit?

source.title: The Future Belongs to Those Who Resist It

movement.gist: Introduce the prompt engineer figure: someone paid to coax useful output from language models by crafting careful instructions, whose job title itself keeps sliding — half technical, half rhetorical — and who is claimed and disowned by multiple departments at once.

Try the category 'programming.' It fits in that prompting is precise, iterative, testable, produces reliable outputs from formal inputs — but the trial mutilates it: prompting has no fixed syntax, no compiler, no guaranteed determinism, and success depends on something more like persuasion than specification.

Try the category 'writing' or 'translation' instead. Prompting resembles composing rhetoric aimed at an audience, or translating intent into another idiom — but this too mutilates it: the 'audience' has no stable interpretive habits, changes weekly with model updates, and the writer's skill evaporates the moment the model is retrained.

Turn from the phenomenon to what the failed trials reveal about taxonomy itself: each category demanded the activity hold still long enough to be measured against a stable exemplar, but the exemplars themselves (compiler, audience, translation-pair) were only ever stand-ins for stability we no longer have; the misfit is not prompting but the assumption that skills must resemble their ancestors to be named.

primary.axis: whether prompting is a species of an existing skill or a genuinely new kind of activity
poles: prompting as a dialect of an established craft (coding, writing, translating, managing)

secondary.axis: whether the difficulty of naming the activity lies in the activity or in the inadequacy of our taxonomic instruments
poles: the activity itself is genuinely hybrid/unstable
our category system simply lacks the right joint to carve at

tension_system.interaction: the secondary tension supplies the mechanism by which the primary one gets dissolved rather than settled — the essay redirects attention from 'what is prompting' to 'why do we need a name for it at all'

family_realization.note: Passage executes 'Category Refugee' flawlessly. Prompting tried against programming (compiler gate fails), rhetoric (audience instability fails), translation (language pair replaced fails). Para 4 reveals the mechanism: categories name fixed correlates, not activities. Ending reframes the inquiry outward.

ending_behavior.note: Performs 'Practical Deflation' well but with slight aperture softness. Grand movement (three failed taxonomies) lands on small reframing: stop naming; audit which fixed objects remain. Phrase 'still sitting where we left them' shows aperture narrowing, though 'how the crafts are faring' reopens slightly rather than staying tight.

voice_consistency.note: Maintains 'Analytic Miniaturist' throughout. Dry wit: 'The slash is the whole story.' Concrete particular: job-title oscillation as symptom. Uneven polish: 'Call it soft code, then' conversational; some sentences abstract but not all. Single-sentence paragraphs create texture.

distractor_efficiency.note: Q1(A): terminological_twin—plausible because vocab does transfer; requires noticing 'soft code' denial. Q2(B): phrase_misuse—canon language echoes para 3, traps readers who skimmed withdrawal. Q3(A): phrase_misuse—mirrors essay structure, reverses its logic. Q5(D): false_symmetry—requires tracking that failures differ. Most traps are content-logic, not lexical.

explanation_quality.note: Consistently names mechanisms tied to line locations. Q1(A): cites compiler passage denying transfer. Q2(A): quotes 'sediment' and version-retraining claim. Q3(B): cites paragraph 4 directly. Q5(A): names inductive-base collapse. Q8(D): traces closing sentence redirection. No 'not mentioned' or extremity judgments; all grounded.

answers.reasoning: Passage argues craft names need fixed correlates; prompting lacks one, so classification fails.
Text directly states skill against v4 is sediment, not skill against v5.
Author explicitly says a fifth name would repeat the error, needing its own fixed correlate.
Inference generalizes from three cases; needs premise that craft names designate fixed objects generally.
Three failed trials establish the pattern; removing one leaves insufficient examples for generalization.
Contrasted with 'skill,' sediment implies inert deposit, not transferable or building craft knowledge.
Compiler's rejection feature becomes the template for the fixed-object argument; B also plausible but less precise.
Final line asks which fixed objects of older crafts still hold, implying broader erosion beyond prompting.
